description: Pasting her own Human invitation into Link this device on the studio Mac shows the headline "This is a Human invitation. Confirm your identity first, then join with it." Following it, the identity form accepts exactly the same name and email as an existing project member without a warning, and the join succeeds as a second person: both boards now show two "Grace Liu" avatars and two "Grace Liu · human" filter entries.
expected: The refusal first asks "Is this your own computer? Ask for a My device invitation instead", and joining with a name/email that matches an existing member warns before creating a duplicate.
actual: The UI steers her into a duplicate identity.
suggested_fix: Reorder the refusal copy to lead with the My device route; warn on duplicate git identity at join.

description: Recovery is CLI-only and leaves permanent residue: the creator must find the duplicate humanId in `client show` and revoke the member; the studio client then cannot link with a My device invitation (IDENTITY_MISMATCH "Destination already belongs to another identity") and needs a fresh data directory, which nothing says. After relinking a fresh client, the revoked duplicate still appears as a second "Grace Liu" (avatar and Assigned to filter) on every board.
expected: A UI path to remove the duplicate and relink, and revoked duplicates hidden or marked.
actual: Fresh directory plus CLI; duplicate visible forever.
suggested_fix: See F-043-01 and F-043-04; also hide revoked members from the avatar stack and filters.

description: The Invite menu tells Human and My device apart only by small detail text ("A person and their agent" vs "Another computer you use"); "Human" reads as "me" to a newcomer, and the explanatory dialog text appears only after choosing.
expected: Menu labels that say whose computer it is, e.g. "Someone else" / "Another of my computers".
actual: Easy to pick Human for one's own second machine.
suggested_fix: Rename the menu items or add a one-line explainer at the top of the menu.
